prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of the Telegram Bot API: messages per second, file upload and download size. Cite Telegram's own documentation or FAQ and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the official Telegram Bot API documentation and FAQ, here are the documented limits for messaging rates and file handling.

### Messaging Rate Limits

Telegram imposes different rate limits depending on the context of the conversation (private chat, group, or bulk broadcast).

SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq/ | QUOTE: "In a single chat, avoid sending more than one message per second." | CLAIM: The recommended limit for sending messages in a single private chat is 1 message per second.
SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq/ | QUOTE: "In a group, bots are not be able to send more than 20 messages per minute." | CLAIM: The limit for sending messages in a group chat is 20 messages per minute.
SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq/ | QUOTE: "For bulk notifications, bots are not able to broadcast more than about 30 messages per second, unless they enable paid broadcasts to increase the limit." | CLAIM: The default limit for bulk notifications (broadcasts) is approximately 30 messages per second.
SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq/ | QUOTE: "Enabling paid broadcasts in @BotFather allows a bot to broadcast up to 1000 messages per second." | CLAIM: Bots can increase their bulk broadcast limit to 1000 messages per second by enabling paid broadcasts, subject to specific balance and user activity requirements.

### File Upload and Download Limits (Official API)

When using the standard Telegram Bot API servers (`api.telegram.org`), there are strict size limits for files.

SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq/ | QUOTE: "Use the getFile method. Please note that this will only work with files of up to 20 MB in size." | CLAIM: The maximum file size that can be downloaded via the `getFile` method on the official API is 20 MB.
SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq/ | QUOTE: "Bots can currently send files of any type of up to 50 MB in size, so yes, very large files won't work for now." | CLAIM: The maximum file size that can be uploaded/sent by a bot on the official API is 50 MB.
SOURCE: https://docs.python-telegram-bot.org/en/v13.10/telegram.constants.html | QUOTE: "`telegram.constants.``MAX_FILESIZE_DOWNLOAD¶ : In bytes (20MB)`" | CLAIM: The python-telegram-bot library constants reflect the 20 MB download limit.
SOURCE: https://docs.python-telegram-bot.org/en/v13.10/telegram.constants.html | QUOTE: "`telegram.constants.``MAX_FILESIZE_UPLOAD¶ : In bytes (50MB)`" | CLAIM: The python-telegram-bot library constants reflect the 50 MB upload limit.

### Local Bot API Server Limits

Telegram provides an open-source Local Bot API Server that developers can host themselves. This server removes or significantly increases many of the limits imposed by the official cloud API.

SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api/ | QUOTE: "Download files without a size limit." | CLAIM: A local Bot API server allows downloading files of unlimited size.
SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api/ | QUOTE: "Upload files up to 2000 MB." | CLAIM: A local Bot API server allows uploading files up to 2000 MB (2 GB).
SOURCE: https://core.telegram.org/bots/features | QUOTE: "| Local | Unlimited | 2000MB | HTTP | Any port | 1-100000 |" | CLAIM: The feature comparison table confirms that the Local API supports unlimited download sizes and 2000 MB upload sizes.
